title: Removing the n ≥ 0 restriction
content: The docstring frames the gap: the parent proved pellNorm(aⁿ) = pellNorm(a)ⁿ and R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) only for natural n, truncating the ℤ-indexed orbit {aⁿ : n ∈ ℤ}. The negative exponents are the conjugate/inverse solutions x − y√d, equally part of the unit group. This file extends both laws to all n ∈ ℤ; the only new ingredient is pellNorm(a⁻¹) = pellNorm(a)⁻¹.
mathContext: $\{a^n : n \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is the full two-sided orbit; $a^{-1} = (x, -y)$ is the conjugate solution.

title: Inherited homomorphism kit
content: Re-derives the parent results the integer-power laws stand on: pellNorm_one (unit), pellNorm_mul (Brahmagupta multiplicativity, via linear_combination clearing (√d)²=d), pellNorm_mul_inv (conjugate identity (x+y√d)(x−y√d)=x²−dy²=1 from a.prop), pellNorm_ne_zero, and pellNorm_pow (natural-power law by induction). Including them keeps the entry self-contained and independently verifiable.

title: Norm of the inverse is the reciprocal
content: pellNorm_inv: pellNorm(a⁻¹) = pellNorm(a)⁻¹. The conjugate identity pellNorm(a)·pellNorm(a⁻¹) = 1 says, in the field ℝ where the norm is nonzero, that pellNorm(a⁻¹) is the multiplicative inverse of pellNorm(a). Proved by field_simp (using pellNorm_ne_zero) followed by linear_combination on pellNorm_mul_inv. This single lemma is exactly what flips the sign of the exponent in the zpow law.

title: Integer-power norm and regulator laws
content: pellNorm_zpow: pellNorm(aⁿ) = pellNorm(a)ⁿ for all n ∈ ℤ. Int.eq_nat_or_neg splits n = ±m; the +m branch is zpow_natCast then pellNorm_pow, the −m branch pushes both the group and real zpow through zpow_neg (Solution₁ d is a group, ℝ a field), rewrites the norm of the inverse with pellNorm_inv, and reduces to pellNorm_pow again. pellRegulator_zpow: take logs with Real.log_zpow — valid for either sign since the norm is nonzero — giving R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) for all n ∈ ℤ, the regulator as a ℤ-linear character.
